title: PPC-spiral measurement infrastructure
description:
Cross-cutting infrastructure that must land before any Tier A–D kernel work. All tasks in SA, SB, SC, SD depend on every task in this story.

## Children (4 tasks)

- **I1** — Pin the current criterion baseline; commit `dev/benchmarks/ppc-baselines.json` mapping each Tier-A–D kernel to its baseline ID and commit hash.
- **I2** — Add `dev/benchmarks/ppc-compare.sh` that runs a kernel bench against its pinned baseline and exits non-zero if geomean speedup < 1.5×. Register `criterion-1.5x` gate in the JIT registry.
- **I3** — Add a per-kernel `*.asm.txt` artefact convention; helper script `dev/scripts/regen-asm.sh <kernel-symbol>` invoking `cargo show-asm`. Register `asm-artefact-present` gate that asserts the sibling artefact was regenerated in the same commit.
- **I4** — Proptest scaffolding: shared helper crate or module providing `assert_simd_matches_scalar(scalar_fn, simd_fn, gen)` for SIMD kernels; word-boundary test list (0/1/63/64/65/127/128/129).

## Why this story exists

The PPC methodology requires a stable baseline + asm inspection + correctness equivalence at every spiral step. Without I1–I4 in place, downstream tasks cannot prove their gains.

## Success criteria

- [hard] `dev/benchmarks/ppc-baselines.json` exists and references actual saved criterion baselines for the targeted bench files.
- [hard] `dev/benchmarks/ppc-compare.sh ANY_KERNEL_ID` runs without modification and exits 0/1 cleanly.
- [hard] New JIT gates `criterion-1.5x` and `asm-artefact-present` are defined in the registry.
- [hard] Proptest helper compiles and is unit-tested with at least one trivial SIMD/scalar pair (the existing `LogicalFns::xor_fn`).
